Work in C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod (a Next.js 16 + Prisma app called Kodely — an AI website builder).

BUILD: free-credit rewards for following Kodely's social accounts.

## The feature
50 credits each for: joining the Discord, following on Instagram, liking the Facebook page, following on LinkedIn. 200 credits total, once per account ever.

## Read this before designing — it is the crux
The owner's instruction was explicit: **do NOT ship an honour-system button that grants credits on click.** Free credits are real model spend on the company card, so a claim must be earned.

Reality per platform (verify this yourself, don't take my word for it):
- **Discord** — genuinely verifiable. OAuth2 `identify` + `guilds` scope, or a bot checking guild membership. This one can be done properly.
- **Instagram / Facebook** — Meta Graph API follower checks are heavily restricted and generally not available for this use case.
- **LinkedIn** — no follower-check API at all.

So build Discord as the real, verified path, and for the other three implement a deliberately weaker "connect + delayed grant" flow that is HONEST about being weaker — clearly separated in the code, with a comment explaining that it is unverifiable and what the abuse exposure is. Do not paper over the difference. If you conclude a platform can't be done responsibly at all, say so in your report and leave it unimplemented rather than faking it.

## Scope — YOU MAY ONLY CREATE/EDIT FILES UNDER `app/api/rewards/`, `components/rewards/`, and `app/settings/`
Everything else is off limits — other agents are working in parallel. Read anything you need.

## Anti-abuse — this is the hard part, treat it as the main deliverable
- The credit ledger (lib/credits.ts — READ ONLY, do not edit) is append-only with a `reason` string. Use a deterministic reason like `reward:discord` as the idempotency key: one grant per platform per user, ever, enforced by checking for an existing ledger row before granting. Read `grantCredits` and `getBalance` to see the shape.
- One grant per EXTERNAL social identity across ALL accounts — otherwise one Discord account feeds fifty signups. You cannot add a Prisma table (schema is owned by someone else), so solve this with what exists: think about what you can encode in the ledger `reason` string, e.g. including a hash of the external account id. Explain your approach and its limits honestly in the report.
- Consider grant velocity: many claims in a short window is the signal that matters.

## UI
A small rewards section in `app/settings/page.tsx` (that file is released to you — an existing `SpendCapForm` component lives beside it; match its visual idiom exactly: `rounded-xl border border-black/10 dark:border-white/10`, `text-sm`, restrained). Show which rewards are claimed vs available. It must degrade gracefully: if the Discord env config is absent, that reward simply doesn't appear rather than erroring.

## Critical constraints
- DO NOT modify: prisma/schema.prisma, lib/credits.ts, lib/agent.ts, lib/agent-sdk.ts, lib/build-site.ts, lib/events.ts, lib/build-narration.ts, lib/auth.ts, app/api/generate/route.ts, app/projects/[id]/Editor.tsx, app/dashboard/**, app/globals.css, proxy.ts, deploy.sh, .env, package.json.
- DO NOT add npm dependencies.
- DO NOT run `npm run build`, `git commit`, `git push`, or `deploy.sh`.
- **NEVER put a secret, token, client id or client secret in code, a comment, or your report.** Read config from `process.env` only (e.g. `KODELY_DISCORD_CLIENT_ID`, `KODELY_DISCORD_CLIENT_SECRET`, `KODELY_DISCORD_GUILD_ID`) and list the env var NAMES the owner will need to set. Do not create or modify .env.
- You cannot test the Discord OAuth flow — there are no credentials here. Make sure the code fails safe and loudly when unconfigured, and be explicit in your report that this path is unexercised.
- Run `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx eslint <your files>`; your files must be clean. Pre-existing errors elsewhere are not yours.

## Report back
What you built per platform, your cross-account identity solution and its honest limits, the env var names needed, what you verified vs. could not, and any platform you decided not to implement.

Inputs may be a website URL, GitHub PR, Figma design or URL, text or brief, existing footage, or music. HyperFrames is the default output framework unless the user explicitly chooses another framework for the deliverable or asks only to record a browser session.
- hyperframes-animation: All animation knowledge for HyperFrames — atomic motion rules, multi-phase scene blueprints, scene transitions, broader motion-design techniques, AND the seven runtime adapters (GSAP default, plus Lottie, Three.js, Anime.js, CSS keyframes, Web Animations API, TypeGPU). Welcome to the Next.js documentation!

## What is Next.js?

Next.js is a React framework for building full-stack web applications. You use React Components to build user interfaces, and Next.js for additional features and optimizations.

It also automatically configures lower-level tools like bundlers and compilers. You can instead focus on building your product and shipping quickly.

Whether you're an individual developer or part of a larger team, Next.js can help you build interactive, dynamic, and fast React applications.

## How to use the docs

The docs are organized into 3 sections:

- [Getting Started](/docs/app/getting-started): Step-by-step tutorials to help you create a new application and learn the core Next.js features.
- [Guides](/docs/app/guides): Tutorials on specific use cases, choose what's relevant to you.
- [API Reference](/docs/app/api-reference): Detailed technical reference for every feature.

Use the sidebar to navigate through the sections, or search (`Ctrl+K` or `Cmd+K`) to quickly find a page.

## App Router and Pages Router

Next.js has two different routers:

- **App Router**: The newer router that supports new React features like Server Components.
- **Pages Router**: The original router, still supported and being improved.

At the top of the sidebar, you'll notice a dropdown menu that allows you to switch between the [App Router](/docs/app) and the [Pages Router](/docs/pages) docs.

### React version handling

The App Router and Pages Router handle React versions differently:

- **App Router**: Uses [React canary releases](https://react.dev/blog/2023/05/03/react-canaries) built-in, which include all the stable React 19 changes, as well as newer features being validated in frameworks, prior to a new React release.

- **Pages Router**: Uses the React version installed in your project's `package.json`.

This approach ensures new React features work reliably in the App Router while maintaining backwards compatibility for existing Pages Router applications.

## Pre-requisite knowledge

Our documentation assumes some familiarity with web development. Before getting started, it'll help if you're comfortable with:

- HTML
- CSS
- JavaScript
- React

If you're new to React or need a refresher, we recommend starting with our [React Foundations course](/learn/react-foundations), and the [Next.js Foundations course](/learn/dashboard-app) that has you building an application as you learn.

## Accessibility

For the best experience when using a screen reader, we recommend using Firefox and NVDA, or Safari and VoiceOver.

## Join our Community

If you have questions about anything related to Next.js, you're always welcome to ask our community on [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions), [Discord](https://discord.com/invite/bUG2bvbtHy), [X (Twitter)](https://x.com/nextjs), and [Reddit](https://www.reddit.com/r/nextjs).

content.text:
## What I built

**Files** (all within scope; nothing else touched — verified with `git status`):
- `C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\app\api\rewards\_lib.ts` — platform-neutral core
- `C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\app\api\rewards\route.ts` — GET status
- `C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\app\api\rewards\discord\start\route.ts`, `...\discord\callback\route.ts` — **verified** path
- `C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\app\api\rewards\social\_unverified.ts`, `...\social\connect\route.ts`, `...\social\claim\route.ts` — **unverified** path
- `C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\components\rewards\RewardsCard.tsx`
- `C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\app\settings\page.tsx` (added the section)

**Discord — genuinely verified.** OAuth2 with `identify` + `guilds.members.read`, then a server-to-server `GET /users/@me/guilds/{guild.id}/member`. 200 = member, 404 = not. I chose this over scanning `/users/@me/guilds` deliberately: that list caps at 200 per page, which is also roughly the account guild cap, so a Nitro user in 200+ servers would get a **false negative** — a real user denied a real reward. It also asks a far narrower consent. Any other status (401/403/429/outage) is treated as inconclusive and fails closed — inconclusive never pays out. Token is used once and never stored.

**Instagram / LinkedIn — unverified, and the code says so.** Self-declared handle → delta-0 pending ledger row → 72h hold → explicit claim. `social/_unverified.ts` opens with a banner comment stating plainly that anyone can type any handle, that the identity rule stops handle *reuse* but not handle *invention*, and that the hold is damage control rather than prevention.

## Facebook: I recommend you do NOT enable it

This is the one I'd flag hardest. Beyond being unverifiable, Meta's developer incentivization policy enumerates what an app may reward and **expressly says not to incentivize people to Like a Page** — "like our Facebook page for 50 credits" is close to a verbatim prohibited example. Separately, `user_likes` App Review has enumerated allowed usages (interest personalization, under-18 parental monitoring) that don't include incentives, and Pages under the New Page Experience report Followers rather than Likes anyway.

I left the code in (it's uniform with the other two) but it is **inert unless someone sets `KODELY_FACEBOOK_URL`**, and the file tells the reader not to set it until a human has read Meta's policy in a browser. My research agent flagged that several Meta policy pages 404'd or served wrong-locale text to automated fetches, so please have someone confirm the exact wording before relying on it. The same caution applies to Instagram, which sits under the same Meta umbrella.

## Cross-account identity — and its honest limits

`reason` carries the whole state machine, since I can't add a table:
- `reward:<platform>:<hash>` — delta +50, a grant
- `reward:<platform>:pending:<hash>` — delta 0, an unverified claim on hold

`hash` is **HMAC-SHA256** of `platform:externalId` keyed by a server secret, truncated to 96 bits — not a plain digest. Discord snowflakes and Instagram handles are low-entropy; an unkeyed digest sitting in a `reason` column would let anyone with DB read access brute-force "is @someuser a customer of yours?". So "has this external identity ever been rewarded, on any account?" is one query, and the ledger leaks nothing.

**Limits, stated plainly:**
- For Discord it's strong — the id comes from Discord, so one Discord account genuinely earns 50 credits once, ever.
- For the other three it stops handle *reuse* only. Fifty accounts each typing a different invented handle each get 50 credits. Exposure is ~$0.30 per fake account across the three unverified platforms (~$0.10 with only Discord+LinkedIn enabled).
- Even Discord is a snapshot: nothing prevents join → verify → leave. The member object carries `joined_at` if you later want a tenure gate.
- Delta-0 rows are safe against `getBalance`/`spentInWindow`, but a build charge committing mid-transaction could still clobber `balanceAfter` — that race is inherent to the ledger's read-then-write shape and predates this work (`grantCredits` and `chargeForBuild` have it too). I fixed rewards-racing-rewards, not the pre-existing one.

**Other gates:** 24h account-age minimum (the farm loop's only uncompressible cost is waiting); a global velocity circuit breaker at 25 grants/hour that refuses grants and logs loudly rather than quietly bleeding credits; and Postgres advisory locks around every ledger write, since there's no unique constraint on `reason` to lean on and a double-submit would otherwise double-spend real money.

## Env vars you'll need to set

`KODELY_REWARDS_ID_SALT` (**required** — random, ≥16 chars; without it *no* reward appears and nothing is ever granted), `KODELY_DISCORD_CLIENT_ID`, `KODELY_DISCORD_CLIENT_SECRET`, `KODELY_DISCORD_GUILD_ID`, `KODELY_DISCORD_INVITE_URL`, `KODELY_INSTAGRAM_URL`, `KODELY_LINKEDIN_URL`, and `KODELY_FACEBOOK_URL` (see the warning above). Register `https://<your-host>/api/rewards/discord/callback` as an authorized redirect URI on the Discord OAuth client. I did not create or modify `.env`.

## Verified vs. not

**Verified:** `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx eslint` both clean. Handle normalization tested against the shipped source — this caught a real bug where `facebook.com/kodely.app` returned null, because my hostname filter was dropping any segment containing a dot and Facebook usernames legitimately contain periods. Advisory-lock SQL tested against your actual Postgres in a rolled-back transaction — this caught a second real bug: I'd "corrected" `$executeRaw` to `$queryRaw`, which throws `Failed to deserialize column of type 'void'` because `pg_advisory_xact_lock` returns void. Reverted, with a comment so nobody re-breaks it. All Prisma query shapes executed read-only against the live schema; confirmed `reward:` doesn't collide with the existing `signup_grant`/`build` reasons.

**Not verified:** the Discord OAuth flow end-to-end — there are no credentials here, so **that path is entirely unexercised**. The token exchange, the member check, and the grant have never run. Please test with a real client against a throwaway guild, checking both the member and non-member cases, before announcing it. I also did not run the dev server: `next dev` rewrites `AGENTS.md`, which is outside my scope.

**One product decision for you:** the unverified path needs the user to return after 72h and click Claim. Auto-granting would mean writing credits as a side effect of a page render, which I wasn't willing to do — but it does mean some users will forget.
